It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing a world that seeks to “remodel the way we think about truth” by adding human opinions to the pure Word of God, and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the sufficiency of Scripture and the impulse to supplement it in this hour? [13, 1341, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the “noise and tumult” of so-called “fresh revelations,” or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the truth that the Master “sovereignly orders everything He has made” through His written testimonies? [13, 20, 1143, 1408, 1532, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many “shave off the edges” of the truth to offer “spiritual placebos” or suggest that the Bible needs the help of “modern psychology,” we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs our souls by His complete and perfect Law [1, 11, 24, 28, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, His Word is a “lavish endowment” that is “wholly sufficient” to direct the life of every believer [15, 68, 1143, 1312, 1331, 1339, 1532, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The All-Sufficient Standard for the Soul**

**Verse**
“ ‘All Scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness, that the man of God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work’ ” (2 Timothy 3:16–17). [922, 1062, 1240, 1263, 1331, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed faith—echoed by **John MacArthur**—asserts that Scripture is “God-breathed” and is the “only source of absolute divine authority” for the believer [922, 1263, 1312, 1331, Conversation History]. The Scripture declares, “ ‘The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul; the testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple; the statutes of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart; the commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes’ ” (Psalm 19:7–8). [860, 1240, 1263, 1330, Conversation History]. Because the Bible is the “inspired Word of Almighty God,” it is “totally sufficient for your needs” and does not require the supplement of “human ingenuity” or “pagan babblers” [21, 1240, 1264, 1312, 1333, 1503, Conversation History]. This “more sure word of prophecy” is the “traveler’s map” that contains “all things that pertain to life and godliness” (2 Peter 1:3; 1:19) [595, 785, 818, 1151, 1328, 1503, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not look for some other fountain of knowledge,” for the Bible is the “only source of divine revelation” that can sustain your “daily walk with God” (James 1:17; Psalm 119:105). [51, 123, 1266, 1333, 1503, Conversation History]. Recognize that “ ‘man shall not live by bread alone; but man lives by every word that proceeds from the mouth of the LORD’ ” (Deuteronomy 8:3). [10, 11, 728, 809, 811, 925, 1261, 1406, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, the “religious leaders” were often “punctilious” about “legal minutiae,” yet they “neglected the weightier matters” and “corrupted the good things God had taught” with their own traditions (Matthew 23:23). [8, 14, 176, 248, 1053, 1352, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our posture, showing that we are now the “pillar and ground of the truth,” where a “mind transformed by the renewing of biblical truth” replaces “ritualized ceremonies” (1 Timothy 3:15; Romans 12:2). [13, 24, 67, 142, 876, 1261, 1284, 1313, 1426, 1445, 1529, 1646, 1694, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: The Peril of Adding Human Traditions**

**Verse**
“ ‘Beware lest anyone cheat you through philosophy and empty deceit, according to the tradition of men, according to the basic principles of the world, and not according to Christ’ ” (Colossians 2:8). [12, 101, 170, 255, 312, 1168, 1254, 1406, 1502, 1551, 1670, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The “record of history” reveals a recurring “human tendency” to “seek to be enlightened” by “cleverly devised myths” rather than the “spotless purity of truth” [4, 28, 439, 453, 1307, 1359, 1391, 1500, 1532, Conversation History]. Jesus rebuked those who supplemented His Word, saying, “ ‘These people draw near to Me with their mouth, and honor Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me. And in vain they worship Me, teaching as doctrines the commandments of men’ ” (Matthew 15:8–9). [1002, Conversation History]. The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Paul Washer**—warns that those who “stitch together a variety of religious ideas” are “spiritual swindlers” who “turn the grace of our God into lewdness” (Jude 4) [161, 354, 1432, 1450, 1502, 1655, Conversation History]. To rely on “psychic intuition” or “subjective feelings” is a “spirit of fraud” that “undermines the authority of Scripture” [11, 122, 186, 317, 343, 345, 348, 598, 1503, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by a “worldly philosophy” that suggests truth is “soft and pliable,” for “your life is not your own” and you must “submit your mind to the truth of Scripture” (1 Corinthians 6:19; 1 John 2:21). [12, 91, 101, 1202, 1262, 1385, 1406, 1502, 1512, 1670, Conversation History]. Recognize that “ ‘he who trusts in his own heart is a fool,’ ” and you must instead “tremble at My word” (Proverbs 28:26; Isaiah 66:2). [11, 24, 87, 91, 172, 209, 251, 851, 1039, 1313, 1381, 1406, 1445, 1503, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Ritual vs. Reality**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “animal sacrifices” and physical sanctuaries were “shadows” that pointed to the Savior but could not “eliminate sin” [11, 13, 32, 142, 394, 911, 1313, 1344, 1345, 1430, 1440, 1442, 1443, 1482, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our worship, revealing that “everything the Sabbath signified has been completely fulfilled in the finished work of Christ,” meaning we find “repose of the soul” not in “ritualized ceremonies” but in “the renewing of your mind” (Hebrews 4:10; Romans 12:2). [13, 17, 24, 136, 142, 157, 446, 860, 876, 1253, 1313, 1426, 1445, Conversation History].

### **Section 3: The Danger of "Itching Ears" and False Knowledge**

**Verse**
“ ‘For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine, but according to their own desires, because they have itching ears, they will heap up for themselves teachers; and they will turn their ears away from the truth, and be turned aside to fables’ ” (2 Timothy 4:3–4). [258, 477, 1461, 1499, 1530, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Scripture handles the “clamor and tumult” of those seeking “fresh revelation” by affirming that “no lie is of the truth,” for the Lord says, “ ‘An astonishing and horrible thing has been committed in the land: The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests rule by their own power; and My people love to have it so’ ” (Jeremiah 5:30–31). [115, 731, 1136, 1266, 1323, 1384, 1406, 1512, 1516, 1605, Conversation History]. The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Voddie Baucham**—notes that “men loved darkness rather than light” because “sin is the monarch that rules the heart,” leading people to seek “spiritual placebos” that “muffle the truth of God’s Word” (John 3:19). [11, 72, 73, 213, 1131, 1336, 1365, 1406, 1483, 1515, Conversation History]. Those with “itching ears” are “tossed to and fro... by the trickery of men” because they “did not receive the love of the truth” (Ephesians 4:14; 2 Thessalonians 2:10). [296, 938, 1341, 1343, 1405, 1420, 1452, 1453, 1506, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You must “discipline your body and bring it into subjection,” ensuring that you “test all things; hold fast what is good” (1 Corinthians 9:27; 1 Thessalonians 5:21). [12, 13, 79, 90, 101, 116, 294, 295, 396, 433, 1017, 1313, 1406, 1408, 1515, 1670, 1709, Conversation History]. “Saturate and renew your mind” with the “more sure Word,” recognizing that “the heart of the wise teaches his mouth” to avoid “empty noise” (Psalm 119:105; Proverbs 16:23). [11, 21, 101, 105, 116, 562, 917, 926, 995, 1313, 1406, 1515, 1684, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Civil vs. Spiritual Jurisdiction**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “false prophecy” was a “capital offense” because it “counseled rebellion against the LORD” and sought to “seduce” the people from the path of life (Deuteronomy 13:5). [95, 517, 554, 728, 732, 904, 1316, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “warfare,” teaching that while we “do not war according to the flesh,” we must “contend earnestly for the faith” using the “sword of the Spirit” to “cast down arguments... raised against the knowledge of God” (2 Corinthians 10:4–5; Jude 3). [13, 21, 32, 43, 92, 113, 201, 723, 727, 728, 750, 760, 805, 808, 932, 1081, 1093, 1099, 1102, 1103, 1109, 1137, 1141, 1158, 1210, 1246, 1268, 1313, 1325, 1334, 1342, 1344, 1349, 1354, 1358, 1364, 1366, 1367, 1389, 1400, 1401, 1402, 1406, 1408, 1410, 1411, 1415, 1440, 1441, 1443, 1451, 1453, 1461, 1462, 1463, 1467, 1479, 1486, 1488, 1490, 1503, 1515, 1520, 1531, 1532, 1537, 1540, 1542, 1546, 1550, 1554, 1601, 1646, 1670, 1720, Conversation History].

### **Section 4: The Finality and Power of the Written Word**

**Verse**
“ ‘For I testify to everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this book: If anyone adds to these things, God will add to him the plagues that are written in this book; and if anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his part from the Book of Life’ ” (Revelation 22:18–19). [1206, 1214, 1256, 1264, 1324, 1331, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The biblical authors resolve the “noise and tumult” of human “building enterprises” by fixating on the “consummation of history,” where “Christ ultimately crushes the kingdoms of men and establishes His own” [13, 20, 21, 23, 24, 31, 103, 136, 1199, 1311, 1315, 1431, 1515, 1524, 1532, 1636, 1720, Conversation History]. Every ruler who seeks to “write themselves into God’s office” by altering His revelation will ultimately be “weighed on the scales and found deficient” (Daniel 5:27). [11, 15, 30, 37, 324, 412, 1061, 1143, 1402, 1450, 1502, 1720, Conversation History]. The “complete body of revelation” provides “repose of the soul” and “total truth” because “everything the Sabbath signified has been completely fulfilled in the finished work of Christ” (Hebrews 4:10). [13, 17, 24, 136, 142, 1255, 1323, 1445, 1503, Conversation History]. “Faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God,” and no “human monument” can replace the “Spirit-inspired Scriptures” (Romans 10:17). [11, 21, 101, 116, 282, 312, 753, 764, 785, 803, 855, 1113, 1133, 1334, 1406, 1503, 1515, 1684, 1709, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Wait for His Son from heaven,” knowing that “the Word of our God stands forever” while all “cleverly devised myths” will “vanish—like smoke they vanish away” (Isaiah 40:8; Psalm 102:3). [11, 14, 24, 32, 35, 37, 39, 43, 63, 94, 121, 201, 453, 789, 836, 940, 976, 1211, 1233, 1241, 1306, 1315, 1408, 1450, 1460, 1515, 1684, 1720, Conversation History]. You should find “tranquility of soul” by resting upon the “surest foundation,” for if God has “magnified Your word above all Your name,” your “inheritance incorruptible” is “secure” (Psalm 138:2; 1 Peter 1:4). [11, 21, 24, 25, 26, 41, 47, 83, 92, 121, 142, 147, 176, 198, 201, 211, 222, 273, 285, 292, 300, 313, 324, 332, 352, 359, 361, 386, 405, 412, 413, 414, 442, 444, 449, 591, 602, 614, 630, 645, 646, 710, 718, 719, 726, 782, 788, 825, 830, 836, 842, 844, 852, 856, 867, 869, 872, 881, 883, 921, 934, 936, 940, 947, 957, 958, 975, 1012, 1016, 1032, 1033, 1035, 1113, 1132, 1138, 1143, 1181, 1183, 1214, 1221, 1225, 1300, 1301, 1306, 1311, 1312, 1313, 1315, 1406, 1407, 1408, 1420, 1426, 1440, 1441, 1445, 1447, 1450, 1502, 1503, 1515, 1532, 1572, 1614, 1646, 1670, 1684, 1720, Conversation History].

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 87, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 291, 297, 300, 311, 324, 325, 332, 361, 405, 413, 414, 424, 444, 449, 591, 834, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

Seventeenth-century Puritan pastor John Preston captured the essence of this danger in these words: If it is performed in a formal or customary and overly manner, you would be as good to omit it altogether; for the Lord takes our prayers not by number but by weight. When it is an outward picture, a dead carcass of prayer, when there is no life, no fervency in it, God does not regard it. Do not be deceived in this, it is a very common deception. It may be a man’s conscience would be upon him, if he should omit it altogether. Therefore, when he does something, his heart is satisfied, and so he grows worse and worse. Therefore, consider that the very doing of the duty is not that which the Lord heeds, but He will have it so performed that the end may be obtained and that the thing for which you pray may be effected.

Here’s what the wayside hearer, the shallow hearer, and the worldly hearer all have in common: They “bring no fruit to maturity” (Luke 8:14). The whole purpose of agriculture is to produce a harvest. Soil that fails to produce a crop is of no value. The hardened wayside will remain perpetually hard, the shallow soil will most likely not be seeded again, and the weedy soil will be burnt. If it cannot be completely cleared, purged of weeds, and cultivated again, it will be abandoned as wasteland.

That would have shattered the Pharisees’ theological sensibilities. But when Jesus said, “I tell you …” He was making it clear that He did not need to quote some eminent rabbi or scribe. He wasn’t drawing doctrine from Jewish tradition; He was speaking with absolute, divine authority. God incarnate, the holy one of Israel, the spotless, sinless Lamb of God, was teaching that in one gracious moment the most extreme sinner can be pronounced instantly righteous without performing any work, without earning any merit, without following any ritual, and with absolutely no righteousness of his own to bring to the table.

The Lord is making a simple argument from the lesser to the greater. This was a typical form of rabbinical teaching. The point is that if a scheming, dishonest, earthly reprobate is shrewd enough to use his stewardship to make friends for such a brief, temporal future, how much more should we use our Master’s resources to make friends for eternity? This is one key way Jesus wants us to be “wise as serpents and harmless as doves” (Matt. 10:16). Mammon is the Aramaic word for “riches.” Jesus refers to money as “the unrighteous mammon” because earthly riches belong to this fallen, transient world. All earthly wealth will one day be burned up. “Riches are not forever” (Prov. 27:24). “The form of this world is passing away” (1 Cor. 7:31). “The end of all things is at hand” (1 Peter 4:7). “The heavens will pass away with a great noise, and the elements will melt with fervent heat; both the earth and the works that are in it will be burned up” (2 Peter 3:10).

As I began to dig down into this buried jewel of the gospel, its pervasive splendor began to dominate my thinking and preaching. Every time and everywhere I addressed the subject, the response was the same—startled wonder. During the same period I was asked to write a book on the “doctrines of grace” that was faithful to the Reformers. Was another one really necessary? Who could improve on Calvin, Luther, the English Puritans, Edwards, or Spurgeon? Certainly not me. I couldn’t hope to add to the clear, complete, and enduring works of past and present theologians on gospel themes. So I struggled to find a reason to write something new, considering what had already been written.

As Paul explained to Timothy: The firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, “The Lord knows those who are His,” and, “Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness.” Now in a large house there are not only gold and silver vessels, but also vessels of wood and of earthenware, and some to honor and some to dishonor. Therefore, if anyone cleanses himself from these things, he will be a vessel for honor, sanctified, useful to the Master, prepared for every good work. Now flee from youthful lusts and pursue righteousness, faith, love and peace, with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart. (2 Tim. 2:19–22)

Paul was not alone in his understanding of God’s electing work in salvation. Other New Testament writers highlighted these very same realities. The author of Hebrews explained that Christ died so that “those who have been called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance” (9:15). James noted that our salvation resulted from “the exercise of His will” when “He brought us forth by the word of truth” (James 1:18). Peter wrote his first epistle “to those . . . who are chosen according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, by the sanctifying work of the Spirit, to obey Jesus Christ and be sprinkled with His blood” (1 Peter 1:1–2).14 John referred to a lady as “chosen” (2 John 1:13). And Jude, similarly, opened his letter with these words: “To those who are the called, beloved in God the Father, and kept for Jesus Christ” (v. 1).
